```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, 
                      eval = TRUE, message = FALSE)
library(cowplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(grid)
```


## Learning Objectives

1. Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate
2. Describe how the size and bias of a sample affects the \alert{sampling distribution}
3. Calculate the \alert{standard error of the mean}
4. Calculate \alert{confidence intervals} using the \alert{standard error of the mean}
5. Know how to correctly interpret \alert{confidence intervals}
6. Display and correctly interpret \alert{error bars} on a graph

## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

Back to our uhu example

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=8, fig.height=3.25, cache=TRUE}

library(magick)
library(grid)

uhu <- image_read("01_activity_uhu/uhu4measure.png") |> 
    image_flop() |> 
    image_resize(geometry = geometry_size_percent(50)) |> 
    image_transparent("white")

uhuloa <- function(loa = 1) {
    par(mar = rep(0, 4))
    plot(0:50, type = "n", axes = FALSE)
    rect(-0.5, 6, 50.5, 13, col = "gray")
    text(0.5, 7, labels = "cm", cex = 0.75)
    
    segments(x0 = 0, y0 = 12, x1 = 50, lwd = 0.5)
    segments(x0 = 0:50, y0 = 10, y1 = 12, lwd = 0.5)
    segments(x0 = (0:49) + 0.5, y0 = 10.75, y1 = 12, lwd = 0.5)
    segments(x0 = seq(0.1, 49.9, by = 0.1), y0 = 11.25, y1 = 12, lwd = 0.25)
    
    text(0:50, rep(11, 51), labels = 0:50, cex = 0.5, pos = 1)
    
    
    xr <- par("usr")[1:2]
    p <- 1
    grid.raster(uhu, x = (0 - xr[1]) / diff(xr), 
                hjust = 0, width = loa * 50 / diff(xr)) 
}


uhuloa(0.8)
```


## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

5 sections produced 5 \alert{samples} from an unknown \alert{population}

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=3}
uhu <- read.csv("data/section_sample_uhu.csv")
uhu <- uhu[uhu$length_cm > 18, ]
uhu$Section <- sprintf("%02d", uhu$Section)
uhu <- uhu[uhu$Section != "NA", ]

uhu_p <- ggplot(uhu, aes(x = Section, y = length_cm, color = Section)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.1) +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    scale_color_viridis_d(alpha = 0.5)

uhu_p
```


## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

We can calculate the \alert{estimate} of the means for each \alert{samples}

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=3}
uhu_pm <- uhu_p + stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar", 
                               width = 0.75, color = viridis::viridis(5))

uhu_pm
```


## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

Look at the collection of all \alert{estimates} of the means 

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=3}
uhu_m <- group_by(uhu, Section) |> 
    summarize(m = mean(length_cm)) |> 
    ungroup() |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = m, y = 0, color = Section)) +
    geom_point(shape = 18, size = 5) +
    scale_color_viridis_d() +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", 
          axis.line.y = element_blank(), 
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), 
          axis.text.y = element_blank()) + 
    ylab("") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 3)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(28.5, 32))


uhu_all <- plot_grid(uhu_pm, uhu_m)
ggsave("04_estimation-01_files/figure-beamer/uhu_all.pdf", device = "pdf", width = 5, height = 3)


```

## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

Now imagine we could collect many **many** **MANY** samples and look at the collection of all their mean \alert{estimates} 

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=3, fig.height=3}
uhu_s <- uhu_m +
    geom_point(data = data.frame(x = rnorm(20, 30.4), 
                                 y = 0, Section = "06"), 
               mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), 
               shape = 18, size = 5, 
               color = "gray", alpha = 0.5)

uhu_s 
```

## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

The \alert{estimated} means of those many **many** **MANY** \alert{samples} come from the \alert{sampling distribution}

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=3.5, fig.height=2.5}
uhu_s + stat_function(fun = \(x) 4 * dnorm(x, 30.25, sd = 0.75), 
                      color = "black") +
    ylab("\"Probability\"") + 
    theme(axis.line.y = element_line())
```

## Describe the \alert{sampling distribution} of an estimate

The \alert{sampling distribution} describes all the possible outcomes (and how likely or unlikely those outcomes are) of taking infinite hypothetical \alert{samples} from the same \alert{population} and calculating an \alert{estimate} (like the mean) for each.


## Describe how the size and bias of a sample affects the \alert{sampling distribution}

* Greater sample size ($N$) decreases variability in the \alert{sampling distribution}
* Biased samples shift the sampling distribution away from the true population parameter

<!-- ## What do you mean by "random sample"? -->

<!-- 1. Samples will differ from true population by random chance (sampling error) -->

<!-- 2. Random sample does not mean every outcome has the same probability -->

<!--     e.g. uhu range in size from roughly 30 cm to 75 cm (in these fake data) but not every value between those extremes are equally likely, medium sizes are more common -->

<!-- *Random means every unit has the same probability of being selected and sampling one unit doesn't effect probability of sampling another* -->

## Greater sample size decreases variability among estimates

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
set.seed(123)
dfsamp <- lapply(c(20, 40, 80), function(n) {
    p <- replicate(1000, {
        s <- rnorm(n, 50, 10)
        mean(s)
    })
    
    data.frame(p = p, n = n)
})

dfsamp <- do.call(rbind, dfsamp)


dfse <- group_by(dfsamp, n) |> 
    summarize(x = mean(p) - 10 / sqrt(n[1]), 
              xend = mean(p) + 10 / sqrt(n[1])) |> 
    ungroup()

dfsamp$n <- paste("n =", dfsamp$n)
dfse$n <- paste("n =", dfse$n)
dfse$y <- dfse$yend <- 50

names(dfsamp)[2] <- names(dfse)[1] <- "Sample size"



sampdp <- ggplot(dfsamp, aes(p)) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(`Sample size`)) +
    geom_histogram(show.legend = FALSE, fill = "gray") + 
    theme_cowplot() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 18)) +
    xlab("Mean length (cm)")

sampdp
```



## The \alert{standard error} quantifies the spread of estimates

> The \alert{standard error} of an estimate is the standard deivation of the estimate's sampling distribution

You can calculate a standard error for any population parameter, but we will start with the standard error of the sample mean

## Standard error of the sample mean

\begin{tabular}{rl}

Sample mean: & $\overline{Y} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i = 1}^n Y_i$ \\

Sample variance: & $s^2 = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i = 1}^n (Y_i - \overline{Y})^2$ \\

Sample standard deviation: & $s = \sqrt{s^2}$ \\

Sample mean \alert{standard error}: & $\text{SE}_{\overline{Y}} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$

\end{tabular}


## Standard error of the sample mean

\begin{tabular}{rl}

Sample mean: & $\overline{Y} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i = 1}^n Y_i$ \\

Sample mean \alert{standard error}: & $\text{SE}_{\overline{Y}} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$

\end{tabular}


The \alert{standard error} is an *estimate* of an **estimate** (e.g. the mean)

As with any estimate we don't know the true value, but it's our best guess


## Greater sample size decreases the \alert{standard error}!!!

```{r fig.align='center', fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
sampdp +
    geom_segment(data = dfse,
                 aes(x = x, y = y, yend = yend, xend = xend), 
                 color = "#DD8739", linewidth = 2) +
    ylab("Count")
```

## Key take-aways:

- \alert{Standard error} describes the spread of the \alert{sampling distribution}
- The \alert{standard error} is the standard deviation of the \alert{sampling distribution}
- The \alert{standard error} is **not** the standard deviation of the data (SE < SD *always*)
- Greater sample size decreases the \alert{standard error}!

## Calculating the \alert{standard error} in *R*

Read in the uhu data you all generated

```{r eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
uhu <- read.csv("data/section_sample_uhu.csv")
```

```{r echo = TRUE}
head(uhu, n = 3)
```


## Calculating the \alert{standard error} in *R*

Calculate estimate of standard deviation for Section 01

```{r echo = TRUE}
# subset data to just section 01
uhu_01 <- subset(uhu, Section == "01")

# calcualte SD
s <- sd(uhu_01$length_cm)
s
```

From `s` we can calculate \alert{standard error}

```{r echo = TRUE}
se <- s / sqrt(length(uhu_01))
se
```
